newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania domestic credits on the rise in May.
newsitem.headline: Romania domestic credits on the rise in May.

text.p: Romania's internal credits rose to 40.4 trillion lei at end-May from 39.4 trillion at the end of April, central bank (BNR) data showed on Monday.
Net credits to the Romanian government slipped by 9.4 percent to 4.4 trillion lei in May, as the State Treasury General Account rose to a 1.2 trillion lei surplus from 789.5 billion lei at end-April.
With banks' lending rates on the slide, non-government credits increased by around one trillion lei to 35.9 trillion, BNR data showed.
According to BNR figures, banks' average lending rates for non-bank customers slipped to an annual 109 percent at end-May from 112.7 percent the previous month.
Hard currency credits went up to the equivalent of 20.7 trillion lei in May from 18.2 trillion at end-April. They took about 58 percent of end-May non-government loans.
Leu credits fell to 15.28 trillion lei at the end of May from 16.4 trillion the previous month, with loans to state companies standing at 8.6 trillion lei, slightly down from 8.8 trillion in April.
End-May credits to private firms dropped to 5.8 trillion lei from 6.79 trillion in April, when total short-term loans accounted for some 83 percent of overall leu loans. ($=7,103 lei)
